title: Maronite Qurbono: bounded manuscript and printed-book stages

traditions.label: Maronite Antiochene Qurbono
traditions.scope: Maronite Eucharistic books in Syriac and native Syriac/Arabic composition; independent vernacular translation history excluded.
traditions.coverage_note: First printing through 2005 with a bounded manuscript precursor and 2003-2006 synodal reception prescriptions. Dates mark attestation/publication/approval, not continuous use. The 2005 stage now rests on the original Arabic decree and introductions read in the 2005 people's volume (Kitab al-Mu'minin); the celebrant's bilingual Syriac/Arabic volumes remain unseen. The 1816 Qozhaya and 1959 states rest on Boutros Gemayel's 1970 description of the printed editions, read on page images; Gemayel also supplies the full 1716 roster beside Dib, Kaufhold, Feulner and the 2005 presentation. The 1959 state is an unofficial practical edition.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat.sir.431 (digitized manuscript)
sources.inspection: Provider image 46 of 67 (acquired whole by the 2026-10-19 lane) viewed on 2026-10-21: the opening with the leaf foliated 45 in Western numerals. Two Syriac passages of the post-institution invocation are encircled in ink with interlinear and marginal marks, and a Latin marginal note of a later hand explains the invocation of the Holy Spirit to make this bread the body of Christ, says that some over-zealous persons removed it, and defends it from the liturgies of Clement, Basil, Chrysostom and James, the Council of Florence and Bellarmine, De sacramento Eucharistiae book 4 chapter 14.
sources.limitations: One opening viewed; the Syriac text was not transcribed and the Latin note was read only in outline (its wording about removal is a tentative reading). The note's citation of Bellarmine places it no earlier than his treatise; the hand is not dated here. Other folios of Vat.sir.431 and the Florence parts of manuscript O were not inspected.

sources.title: Missale Syriacum juxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Syrorum Maronitarum (Rome, Komarek, 1762), Austrian National Library 22.D.32 ALT PRUNK
sources.inspection: Provider images (acquired whole by the 2026-10-19 lane) viewed on 2026-10-21: canvas 430 Latin title (Romae MDCCLXII, Komarek); canvas 3 approbation of J. S. Assemani dated 10 April 1763; canvas 363 Imprimatur leaf; anaphora headings in red Serto on canvases 226, 196, 183, 156, 137, 116, 103 and 094, each followed by its institution narrative in large type (canvases 221/220, 192/191, 177/176, 152/151, 133/132, 113/112, 101/100, 089/088); running heads of canvases 040-416; Good Friday heading on canvas 072; Garshuni printer's note on canvas 4. sources.title: Boutros Gemayel, al-Quddas al-Maruni: durus wa-nusus, part 1 (Beirut 1970; imprimatur Ignatius Ziadé, Archbishop of Beirut, 15 February 1970); Internet Archive item unset0000unse_t9k0

Provider OCR used only to find pages.

Gemayel describes the editions he examined (for 1763 a copy in the Oriental Library, Beirut) but gives few page loci in them; his descriptions are not collation performed here. His list of the five anaphoras omitted in 1763 conflicts with the inspected ONB copy on one name.

stages.label: Manuscript O before Roman editing
stages.scope: Source manuscript identified by Jabbour, including the pre-editing institution and epiclesis layers; not all precursors of the print.
stages.witness_label: Mikhail al-Rizzi’s manuscript O: Florence BNCF Cl.III.79 and Cl.III.74, with Vatican Vat.sir.431; colophon BNCF Cl.III.74 f 154r–v.
stages.summary: A divided 1566 missal used in preparing the first print; supplements also contributed.

evidence.claim: Reassembles gatherings of O across the three shelfmarks; the print also uses other material.

The Vatican part of the reconstructed manuscript shows encircled invocation passages and a Latin marginal note on the epiclesis on the folio Jabbour cites (f. 45r); the marked Syriac was not transcribed, so its correspondence to Jabbour's correction layers is not checked here.

stages.limitations: Reconstruction attributed to Jabbour; surviving manuscripts and colophon not inspected. It is not a complete uncontested single-parent genealogy. 2026-10-21: one Vatican opening (f. 45) was inspected; the Florence parts and the colophon remain uninspected.
stages.reception: Maronite manuscript provenance; date of its dispatch to Rome is disputed. The later printed uniform formula must not be projected back over all manuscript layers.

stages.label: First print with revised institution and epicleses
stages.scope: Roman first printing, bounded by checked paratext and source-described liturgical revision.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae nationis Maronitarum, Romae in Typographia Medicea; IA bub_gb_5Eqy8WGF9aQC.
stages.summary: Fourteen anaphoras; Sixtus first and Sharar included. Institution wording standardized; epiclesis petitions altered.

evidence.claim: Latin 1594 and Syriac 1592 dates coexist in this physical witness; 1594 dedication and examiner colophon are visible.
Describes fourteen anaphoras and alteration of institution and epiclesis.
Identifies Sixtus first and the inclusion of Sharar.

stages.limitations: Liturgical body not transcribed or collated. Dual title dates do not establish two successive textual states.
stages.reception: Dib reports introduction at the 1596 synod with Dandini. Beggiani records initial prohibition and later permission while manuscript formulas continued locally; neither account proves universal immediate replacement.

stages.label: Reprint variant replacing commemorated names
stages.scope: Specific diptych/commemoration revision in Jabbour’s beta group; not every 1608 copy.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum 1608 reimpressions, beta group in Jabbour’s comparison; BnF RES M-B-3 is a separately identified 1608 reissue, not assigned here to beta.
stages.summary: One 1608 group substitutes Maron, Antony, Jacob and Ephrem for earlier commemorated names.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes alpha copies marking names from beta copies substituting them.
Confirms a 1608 reimpression with textual changes and new Du Perron preface.

stages.limitations: No 1608 copy independently collated. Jabbour warns that editions may be impressions; alpha/beta is his analytical grouping, not a new universal liturgical edition.
stages.reception: Presence in surviving copies establishes a printed variant; no community-wide reception date established.

stages.label: Roman-derived anaphora and Good Friday adaptation
stages.scope: Second Roman missal revision described in multiple histories.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Maronitarum, Rome, Propaganda Fide 1716.
stages.summary: Fourteen items in the roster according to Dib, the 2005 presentation and Gemayel's table, counted as thirteen anaphoras followed by the signing-of-the-chalice order by Gemayel; Feulner counts thirteen. The roster changes: Roman Church added (in place of Marutha), John Maron added (in place of John bar Shushan), a second, different Chrysostom text replaces the first; Sharar removed as an anaphora and adapted as the Good Friday signing of the chalice.

evidence.claim: Reports altered roster, fourteen total, Roman Church and Sharar-derived Good Friday order.
Explains adaptation of Roman Canon material to the structure of Twelve Apostles.

Quotes the 1716 preface on compiling a Roman Church anaphora, placing John Maron's anaphora last and the Sharar-derived signing of the chalice after the anaphoras; gives the contents as the Mass with thirteen anaphoras then the signing-of-the-chalice anaphora, Gospel selections (103) and weekday Epistles; tabulates the first-edition roster of fourteen against the second edition's retentions and replacements; reports printing in Rome 1715 with a closing note dating completion to 1716.

Official retrospective: the second printing of 1716 also had fourteen, dropping three of the first printing and adding John Maron, Roman Church and a different Chrysostom text, and turned Sharar into the Mass of the signing of the chalice.

stages.limitations: No 1716 page images inspected; the roster is from scholarship (Gemayel's full table, Kaufhold's partial copy description, Feulner) and two official retrospectives. Thirteen versus fourteen corresponds in Gemayel's description to whether the signing-of-the-chalice order is counted, but Dib and Feulner do not state their basis. Gemayel quotes the preface as placing the Roman Church anaphora after Xystus; the full printed order is not settled here. The Roman Church anaphora should not be described merely as an unchanged translation of the Roman Canon.
stages.reception: Publication and later reception are distinct. Synodal debates about institution wording do not independently identify a new missal state.

stages.label: Reduced anaphora repertoire
stages.date_label: 1762 title imprint; approbation 10 April 1763 (same copy); 1763 in the official introduction
stages.scope: Third Roman edition with smaller repertoire; disputed exact count retained.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum juxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Syrorum Maronitarum, Rome, Komarek 1762 (approbation 10 April 1763); ONB 22.D.32 ALT PRUNK.
stages.summary: Repertoire reduced from the 1716 book. The inspected copy carries eight anaphora headings, each with its own institution narrative: Peter head of the Apostles, Twelve Apostles, Xystus, John, Mark, Eustathius, the holy Roman Church and John Maron. A separate Good Friday order headed as the anaphora of the signing of the holy chalice follows them. Gemayel describes the edition as a reprint of 1716 at the Antonine order's expense omitting five anaphoras, with Gospel texts at their place in the Mass and a liturgical year beginning with the Sunday of the Consecration of the Church. Dib and Beggiani count nine; the 1992 introduction counts eight.

evidence.locus: Canvas 430 title; canvas 3 approbation; anaphora headings canvases 226, 196, 183, 156, 137, 116, 103, 094; Good Friday heading canvas 072 with running heads 040-071
evidence.claim: Title 1762 and approbation 1763 stand on one copy; the book has eight anaphoras with institution narratives and a separately headed Good Friday chalice-signing order.
Dates third edition 1762–63 and counts nine.
Counts nine and identifies first anaphora as Second Peter.
Reports eight for 1763.
The printer's note dates completion of printing in Rome to 2 Nisan (April) under Clement XIII, year read tentatively as 1763; canvas 116 heads the anaphora of Eustathius.

Third edition 1763 (a copy in the Oriental Library, Beirut): preface says the 1716 book was exhausted and the Antonine procurator Fr Thomas reprinted it at the order's expense; five anaphoras omitted (Matthew the Shepherd, Dionysius, Eustathius, John Chrysostom, Cyril); closing note dates completion to 2 April 1763; Assemani's approbation of 10 April 1763; not sealed by the patriarch; Gospels placed in the Mass and year beginning with Consecration Sunday.

stages.limitations: Eight anaphoras plus the Good Friday item are what the inspected copy contains. Gemayel's count of five omissions leaves the same total, but he names Eustathius among the omitted, while the ONB copy has an Eustathius heading (canvas 116, re-viewed) and no heading for James; this is either an error in one account or a variant issue, and is not resolved. That a count of nine includes the Good Friday item is compatible but not stated by Dib or Beggiani. The approbation's statement of agreement with 1716 is a doctrinal approval formula, not evidence of an unchanged repertoire. The lectionary and calendar arrangement rests on Gemayel and was not checked on the ONB images. Body text not transcribed; one copy, variant issues unchecked.
stages.reception: Subsequent Lebanese printings are reported; continuity of every wording or rubric has not been collated.

stages.label: Qozhaya printing with appended daily Gospel selections
stages.scope: Lebanese reprint line of the 1763 text at the press of St Anthony, Qozhaya, as described by Gemayel; lectionary and calendar arrangement only.
stages.witness_label: Qurbono (Liber oblationis), press of the monastery of St Anthony Qozhaya, Lebanese monks, 1816; the 1838, 1855 and 1872 Qozhaya printings are reported as reprints of the same line.
stages.summary: Reprints the 1763 liturgical texts with small linguistic corrections, appends Gospel selections for every day of the year after Germanos Farhat, and begins the year with January and the first Sunday after Epiphany instead of the Sunday of the Consecration of the Church; among other small changes of the Qozhaya printings, the patriarch's name takes the place of the Roman approvals, illustrated by Gemayel only from the 1838 colophon.

evidence.claim: Fourth to seventh editions (1816, 1838, 1855, 1872) from the Qozhaya press copy the third edition's texts with simple linguistic corrections and a changed movable-feast table, append daily Gospel selections after Farhat, change the start of the year, keep the older front calendar alongside Farhat's saints, and name the patriarch (1838 colophon quoted).

stages.limitations: No Qozhaya copy inspected; the change is source-described by Gemayel, who does not say in which of the four printings the Gospel appendix first appears beyond grouping them as the fourth edition onwards. The 1838, 1855 and 1872 printings are not counted as further states. Cold review 2026-10-22: Gemayel ties the January year start explicitly to the fourth edition onward, but the Gospel appendix and the replacement of the Roman approvals are features of the Qozhaya group, the latter shown only from 1838.
stages.reception: Printed by the Lebanese monks with the patriarch's permission according to the quoted 1838 colophon; not sealed by the patriarch (Gemayel p. 65). Local use is not established.

stages.label: Dibs order with Roman Church first
stages.scope: Dibs’s reorder, witnessed bibliographically by 1888 and 1908; no separate 1908 revision established.
stages.witness_label: Yusuf al-Dibs, Beirut missal 1888; Ketābā de-qurbānā, al-Maṭbaʿa al-Mārūnīya 1908, second printing.
stages.summary: Roman Church replaces Peter at the head of the anaphora sequence; the 1908 printing has the same eight anaphoras as 1762 in a new order. Dibs's preface, as quoted by Gemayel, also reports Arabic translation of the rubrics and added directions taken from Latin books, a revised Arabic rendering of the audible prayers and readings, preparation and thanksgiving prayers, and an annual calendar for 1889-2000.

evidence.claim: Second Peter leads the preceding edition; Debs 1888 places Roman Church first.
Identifies the 1908 second printing and its retained title page.
Order in the 1908 printing: Roman Church, Peter, Twelve Apostles, Mark, John, Xystus, Eustathius, John Maron.

Eighth edition, Maronite Press Beirut 1888, by Archbishop Joseph Dibs after consulting Patriarch Paul Mas'ad; quotes the preface: Roman anaphora placed first with the common prayers, rubrics translated from Syriac into Arabic, directions from Latin books added, Gospel/Epistle translations revised, Augustinian preparation and thanksgiving prayers, calendar 1889-2000; ninth edition 1908 identical except for added celebration directions (Manara).

stages.limitations: 1888 itself not seen; its contents come from Dibs's preface as quoted by Gemayel and from Beggiani. Gemayel states that the 1908 printing matches 1888 in everything except the added directions, which is consistent with the 1908 anaphora order being that of 1888, but he lists no anaphora orders; the moves of Xystus, Mark and John are observed only between the 1762 and 1908 witnesses. The 1888 date is publication, not the duration of use. Cold review 2026-10-22: Gemayel (p. 61) judges that this edition changed nothing of substance beyond correcting wording, putting the Roman anaphora first and multiplying Latin-style directions; Dibs's preface says he neglected some prayers and blessings and abbreviated others, and the monthly calendar was only translated into Arabic with its feasts unchanged. The added components record these preface-described features, not a reform.
stages.reception: Dibs reports consulting the patriarch; Gemayel notes that no edition bears the patriarch's seal. The 1908 printing is a witness to the Dibs line, not a separately proved reform.

stages.label: Unofficial practical edition in Arabic script
stages.scope: Unofficial practical edition described by Gemayel; changes to rubrics, ordinary prayers and end matter, not a new anaphora repertoire.
stages.witness_label: Tenth edition of the Maronite Mass book, Al-Karim press of the Lebanese Missionaries (Jounieh), 1959, as described by Gemayel; title page not seen.
stages.summary: Drops the prefaces, prints all Garshuni in Arabic script, shortens or removes rubrical directions, puts some hymns and prayers in Arabic, deletes some prayers (the Proemion and first Sedro of the first office, the incense prayer for the dead at the end of Mass, some closing prayers), adds feast psalms before the Epistle, and drops the end matter (preparation and thanksgiving prayers, blessings and the annual calendar). Gemayel calls it a hasty commercial practical printing that spread to almost all churches without official permission.

evidence.claim: Lists the differences of the 1959 tenth edition from the previous edition and describes its uncertain authority.
Printed by the Lebanese Missionary Fathers of Jounieh in 1959; replaced Garshuni with Arabic; never received official approval.

stages.limitations: The 1959 book was not seen; the changes are Gemayel's description. Not a new recension of the anaphoras; whether any material was newly composed in Arabic is not established. Cold review 2026-10-22: kept as a documented state because the book-state layer admits an identifiable edition without an approval act and Gemayel's paged description shows changes to rubrics, prayers and end matter beyond the script change; it is not an approved book, unlike the bkerke2005 stage on another deferred candidate, and must not be read as an authorized Maronite missal.
stages.reception: Gemayel reports that copies carry different or no authorizations, that some bishops forbade its use, and that it nevertheless spread to almost all churches; Beggiani says it never received official approval. No approval act is claimed.

stages.label: Roman experimental proposal

stages.label: Reformed six-anaphora Qurbono
